answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because wander only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, cedar is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any sonnet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
